claim: A bounded Gate 0 architecture and task decomposition plan can be established that addresses the fixed requirements R1-R7, identifies actual migration seams, behavior risks, and missing QA evidence based on the current source inventory and contract constraints.
rationale: The contract sets fixed requirements (R1-R7) including strict game timing (100 nights, each 13 seconds), entity counts (enemies, companions, bosses), and performance/animation frame minimums. Source inventory reveals a monolithic global game state, direct canvas drawing, and inconsistent timing intervals incompatible with the required deterministic 13-second clock, indicating key migration seams. Companion abilities require explicit activation, conflicting with requirement R3 for auto companion abilities, necessitating redesign. The animation frame registry is incomplete, posing a behavior risk relative to R6. The lack of a boss/elite reroll economy and verified 9+9+9 campaign victory evidences missing features directly tied to R4 and R7. The job hierarchy shows dependencies and deliverables aligned to incrementally address these issues over Gates 0 through 6. Gate 0 must produce architecture ADR, module manifest, source migration plan, risk/performance budget, and test inventory, bounding the scope to planning and identifying risks without code changes or testing, consistent with evidence constraints.
objections: The plan assumes all R1-R7 can be fully addressed through incremental gates, which may underestimate complexity in retrofitting monolithic code.
Uncertainty remains on the integration feasibility of new features like auto companion abilities and deterministic clock given legacy constraints.
No explicit source code evidence confirms that the existing 9+9+9 cumulative final interpretation is fully provisional but could be hard to adapt without gameplay regressions.
QA coverage is currently incomplete; risk that test inventory may not capture all behavior and performance risks due to legacy architecture complexity.

decisions: Approve bounded architecture ADR defining module boundaries to migrate from monolithic global state and direct canvas drawing.
Define deterministic 13-second clock as central scheduling mechanism replacing multiple timing intervals.
Design companion ability system rework to support auto activation responding to game events for R3 compliance.
Implement animation frame registry completion to satisfy minimum frame counts and ensure visual consistency.
Specify boss and elite reroll economy mechanisms to enable verified 9+9+9 campaign victory conditions.
Establish comprehensive test inventory covering timing, AI behavior, animation frames, reroll economy, and victory conditions.
Develop risk/performance budget highlighting behavior migration seams and animation performance hotspots.
deliverables: Architecture ADR detailing modular separation and migration seams focusing on legacy monolith decoupling.
Module manifest enumerating discrete subsystems (timing, AI, companion skills, animation, economy).
Source migration plan mapping legacy functions to new modules and identifying required refactor targets.
Risk and performance budget highlighting critical behavior risks and potential bottlenecks.
Test inventory specifying automated and manual test requirements for timing accuracy, AI correctness, animation completeness, reroll economy, and victory verification.
Gate 0 milestone report summarizing analyses and planning outcomes consistent with fixed R1-R7 requirements.
risks: Legacy monolithic code challenging modular migration leading to integration complexity.
Incomplete animation frame data risking visual or gameplay regressions.
Behavioral inconsistencies arising from timing changes to deterministic 13s clock.
Uncertainty in companion skill auto-activation design complexity and player experience.
QA gaps due to insufficient automated tests targeting new reroll economy and campaign victory verification.
next_steps: Conduct detailed source code review to map current timing and AI logic to new modular components.
Engage domain experts to specify companion ability auto activation APIs.
Draft architecture ADR and module manifest with clear boundaries and migration seams.
Inventory existing automated tests and identify gaps relevant to R1-R7.
Prioritize risk/performance analysis focusing on timing consistency and animation frame completeness.
Present Gate 0 deliverables for producer review before Gate 1 design work begins.

required_evidence: Detailed source code function mappings showing timing mechanisms and monolithic dependencies.
Current companion ability function implementations indicating explicit activation.
Animation frame registry data and counts confirming incompleteness against required minimums.
Data on existing boss/elite spawn and reroll mechanisms or absence thereof.
Test coverage reports demonstrating existing QA limitations.
Job role deliverables and dependencies demonstrating planned gate-based modular progression.
